How reliable are they?


These numbers come from the same 7,437 held-out test reviews that none of the models saw during training or tuning.






    
  
  • The fine-tuned DistilBERT made 497 mistakes, the baseline 668 and the frozen-embedding model 1,419.
    • 
  
  • The embedding model reads only the first 256 tokens. Its accuracy drops from 84.4% on shorter reviews to 76.3% on longer ones, while DistilBERT barely changes (93.9% to 92.6%).
    • 
  
  • Of DistilBERT’s 497 errors, 267 were also baseline errors and 329 were also embedding errors. Reviews that fool all three are often sarcastic, mixed or mislabeled.
    • 
  
  • The models were trained only on English IMDB movie reviews, so expect weaker results on other kinds of text. Results come from a single seed, and a GPU retrain moved DistilBERT’s accuracy by about 0.02 points.
    •
